title: Clonal expansion within pneumococcal serotype 6C after use of seven-valent vaccine.
ehr_evidence: All serotype 6C invasive disease isolates (n = 4) from blood or cerebrospinal fluid specimens received by the HPA South East regional microbiology laboratory between 2006 and 2010 were included; these were all from adult patients. To obtain pneumococcal carriage isolates, nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from children aged four years and under.
summary: A whole-genome sequencing study of 19 S. pneumoniae serotype 6C isolates (15 carriage, 4 invasive disease) from Southampton, England, investigating clonal expansion of serotype 6C following introduction of the seven-valent conjugate vaccine (PCV7).
key_findings: Serotype 6C isolates fell into four broad phylogenetically distinct lineages, with the largest clonal complex (CC395/ST1692) comprising twelve of the 19 genome-sequenced isolates.
SNPs separating each isolate from the reference strain SOT2073 ranged from 8 to 19,829, with up to 367 SNPs within the CC395 clonal complex.
The 6C capsular locus was introduced into multiple lineages by independent capsular switching events, yet rapid clonal expansion occurred within a single MLST clonal complex (CC395).
All CC395 isolates carried a lantibiotic synthesis locus not seen in any other serotype 6C sequence type, likely contributing to clonal fitness and expansion.
Serotype 6C carriage increased approximately fourfold after PCV7 introduction, from 3.8% of all isolates in winter 2006/7 to 13.5% and 13.7% in winters 2007/8 and 2008/9.
One isolate (SOT2029, ST3460) showed resistance to erythromycin and tetracycline, carrying ermB and tetM genes.
study_design: Cross-sectional genomic epidemiology study of bacterial isolates
population: Children aged four years and under (nasopharyngeal carriage) and adult patients (invasive disease) from Southampton, England
limitations: Single geographical site (Southampton, England), limiting generalisability.
Small sample size of 19 genome-sequenced isolates.
No demographic data (health, vaccination status, gender, ethnicity) were collected for carriage isolates.
